teach.title: Relations, domain, and range
text: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). The domain is the set of all x-values (inputs). The range is the set of all y-values (outputs).
List each number once, in order, even if it repeats in the pairs.

example.problem: Find the domain and range of {(1, 4), (3, 4), (5, 9)}
steps: Domain: the first numbers are 1, 3, 5. Domain = {1, 3, 5}.
Range: the second numbers are 4, 4, 9. List 4 once. Range = {4, 9}.

teach.title: What makes a function
text: A function is a relation where every input has exactly one output.
Two different x-values may share a y-value. But one x-value may never be paired with two different y-values.

steps: Check each x-value: 2, 3, and 4 each appear once.
Each input has one output, so it is a function. The repeated y-value 5 is fine.

questions.prompt: What is the domain of {(1, 2), (3, 4), (5, 6)}?
questions.hint: The domain is the set of x-values, the first number in each pair.
questions.solution: The first numbers are 1, 3, and 5. The domain is {1, 3, 5}.

questions.prompt: Relation: {(2, 5), (4, −1), (7, 3), (9, 0)}. What is the largest number in the range?
questions.hint: The range is the second number in each pair.
questions.solution: The range is {5, −1, 3, 0}. The largest is 5.

choices: Yes, because every x-value has exactly one y-value
No, because the x-values are not consecutive
Yes, but only because the y-values are all positive
questions.hint: Look at the x-values. Does any x-value appear twice?
questions.solution: The x-values 1, 2, and 4 each appear once, so each has exactly one output. It is a function. Repeating y-values is allowed.

choices: Yes, because there are three pairs
No, because x = 2 is paired with two different y-values
Yes, because the y-values are all different
No, because y = 1 and y = 4 differ by 3
questions.hint: Check whether any input shows up more than once with different outputs.
questions.solution: The input 2 is paired with both 1 and 4. One input with two outputs means it is not a function.

questions.prompt: Relation: {(−3, 4), (0, 4), (5, −2), (8, 1)}. Find the sum of all the numbers in the domain.
questions.hint: The domain uses the x-values only.

questions.prompt: Which relation is NOT a function?
questions.hint: Hunt for an x-value that appears twice with different y-values.
questions.solution: In {(4, 1), (5, 2), (4, 3)}, the input 4 goes to both 1 and 3. The other three have all different x-values, so they are functions.

questions.prompt: {(1, 4), (2, 6), (3, 8)} is a function. You add the pair (2, k) and it must still be a function. What must k be?
questions.hint: The input 2 already has an output.
questions.solution: The input 2 is already paired with 6. For it to stay a function, 2 can only have the output 6. So k = 6.

questions.hint: The range is the y-values. Include the 0.
questions.solution: The second numbers are 0, 1, 4, 9. The range is {0, 1, 4, 9}.

teach.title: Mapping diagrams
text: A mapping diagram draws arrows from each input to its output. Here we write the arrows as 2 → 5.
It is a function when every input has exactly one arrow leaving it. Two inputs can point to the same output.

example.problem: Mapping: 1 → 6, 2 → 6, 3 → 9. Is it a function?
steps: Each input 1, 2, 3 has exactly one arrow.
Two inputs sharing the output 6 is allowed.
It is a function. Domain {1, 2, 3}, range {6, 9}.

teach.title: Tables
text: A table is a list of ordered pairs. Read each column pair as (x, y).
Look down the x column. If an x-value repeats with different y-values, it is not a function.

example.problem: x: 1, 2, 3, 2 and y: 4, 5, 6, 7. Is it a function?

questions.prompt: Mapping: 1 → 4, 2 → 4, 3 → 7. Is this a function?
choices: Yes, because each input has exactly one arrow
No, because the outputs are not in order
questions.hint: Count the arrows leaving each input, not the arrows entering each output.
questions.solution: Inputs 1, 2, and 3 each have one arrow. Two inputs sharing an output is allowed. It is a function.

questions.prompt: Mapping: 1 → 4, 1 → 6, 2 → 7. Is this a function?
choices: Yes, because each output appears once
Yes, because there are three arrows
No, because the input 1 has two arrows
questions.hint: Does any input have more than one arrow?
questions.solution: The input 1 goes to both 4 and 6. An input with two outputs means it is not a function.

questions.prompt: Table: x = −2, −1, 0, 1 and y = 5, 3, 1, −1. What y-value goes with x = 0?
questions.hint: Find x = 0 in the top row, then read the y-value in the same column.

questions.prompt: Table: x = 1, 2, 3, 2 and y = 5, 6, 7, 8. Is it a function?
choices: Yes, because all the y-values are different
No, because x = 2 has two different y-values, 6 and 8
No, because the x-values are not in order
Yes, because there are four pairs
questions.hint: Write out the pairs. Which x-value repeats?
questions.solution: Pairs: (1, 5), (2, 6), (3, 7), (2, 8). The input 2 gives both 6 and 8, so it is not a function.

questions.prompt: Mapping: 2 → 9, 4 → 9, 6 → 1, 8 → 3. How many different numbers are in the range?
questions.hint: Count each output once, even if two arrows land on it.
questions.solution: The outputs are 9, 9, 1, 3. The different ones are 9, 1, 3. That is 3 numbers.

questions.prompt: Table: x = 4, 7, 7, 10 and y = 1, 2, 3, 4. What is the domain?
questions.hint: The domain is the x-values. Do not list a value twice.
questions.solution: The x-values are 4, 7, 7, 10. List 7 once. The domain is {4, 7, 10}.

questions.prompt: Table: x = 2, 5, 8, k and y = 1, 4, 4, 0. Which value of k makes this table NOT a function?
questions.hint: You need k to match an x-value already in the table, with a different y-value.
questions.solution: With k = 5, the pairs are (5, 4) and (5, 0). The input 5 has two outputs, so it is not a function. The other choices are new x-values.

questions.prompt: Which table represents a function? (Each table lists x, then y.)
questions.hint: Rule out any table with an x-value that appears twice with different y-values.
questions.solution: The first table has (1, 3) and (1, 5). The third has (0, 2) and (0, 4). The fourth has (7, 1) and (7, 3). Only x: 2, 3, 4 and y: 6, 6, 6 has all different inputs, so it is the function.

teach.title: Vertical line test
text: If any vertical line crosses a graph in more than one point, that x-value has two outputs. The graph is not a function.
If every vertical line crosses at most once, it is a function.

example.problem: Does y = x² pass the vertical line test?
steps: Picture any vertical line, like x = 2. It crosses the parabola once, at (2, 4).
Every vertical line crosses once, so it is a function.

teach.title: Domain and range from a graph
text: Domain: how far left and right the graph goes. Range: how far down and up it goes.
A line that goes on forever in both directions has domain and range of all real numbers.

example.problem: Find the range of y = |x|
steps: The graph is a V with its point at (0, 0).
The lowest y-value is 0 and it goes up forever.
Range: y ≥ 0. Domain: all real numbers.

questions.prompt: Does this graph pass the vertical line test? What does that tell you?
choices: No, it is not a function
Yes, but only on one side of the y-axis
It is a relation but cannot be a function
questions.hint: Imagine a vertical line sliding across. Does it ever hit the curve twice?
questions.solution: Every vertical line crosses the parabola exactly once. It passes the test, so it is a function.

questions.prompt: What is the range of the graphed function?
questions.hint: Range is about y. What is the lowest point of the V?
questions.solution: The lowest point is (0, 0). The graph goes up forever. The range is y ≥ 0.

questions.prompt: The graph is a straight line that continues forever in both directions. What are its domain and range?
choices: Domain all real numbers, range y ≥ −3
Domain x ≥ 0, range all real numbers
Domain and range are both all real numbers
questions.hint: A non-horizontal line keeps going left, right, up, and down.
questions.solution: The line extends forever in both directions and covers every y-value. Domain and range are both all real numbers.

questions.prompt: What is the lowest y-value on the graph of y = x² − 4?
questions.hint: Look at the bottom of the curve, the vertex.
questions.solution: The vertex is at (0, −4). The curve opens up, so −4 is the lowest y-value. The range is y ≥ −4.

questions.prompt: What is the domain of y = √x shown in the graph?
questions.hint: Domain is about x. Where does the graph start, and does it include that point?
questions.solution: The graph starts at (0, 0), which is included, and goes right forever. The domain is x ≥ 0.

questions.prompt: The range of y = −x² + 9 is y ≤ k. What is k?
questions.hint: This parabola opens down. Find the highest point.
questions.solution: The vertex (0, 9) is the highest point and the curve opens down. The range is y ≤ 9, so k = 9.

questions.prompt: A vertical line crosses a graph at two different points. What does this mean?
choices: The graph is a function with a repeated output
The graph is not a function
The graph is a function with a repeated input
questions.hint: A vertical line sits at one x-value.
questions.solution: A vertical line fixes one x-value. Two crossing points means that x has two different y-values. So the graph is not a function.

questions.prompt: What is the domain of the graphed function y = 1/x?
questions.hint: The curve never touches the y-axis. Which x-value is missing?
questions.solution: There is no point with x = 0, because you cannot divide by zero. The domain is every real number except 0, so x ≠ 0.

teach.title: Functions from rules and situations
text: An equation is a function if each x gives only one y. Equations like y = 2x + 1 are functions. A vertical line like x = 4 is not.
If a rule is given with a domain, plug in each domain value to find the range.

example.problem: Domain {−1, 0, 2} and rule y = 3x − 1. Find the range.

questions.prompt: Which equation does NOT describe y as a function of x?
questions.hint: Think about the graph. Which one is a vertical line?
questions.solution: x = 4 is a vertical line. The x-value 4 is paired with every y, so it fails the vertical line test. The other three give one y for each x.

questions.prompt: What is the range of y = x² − 1?
questions.hint: x² is never negative. What is the smallest value of x² − 1?
questions.solution: The smallest x² is 0, giving y = −1. Everything above is reachable. The range is y ≥ −1.

questions.prompt: A taxi charges $3 plus $2 per mile. The domain is the whole-number miles 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. How many ordered pairs are in this function?
questions.hint: There is one pair for each domain value. Count them carefully, starting at 0.
questions.solution: Each of the six inputs 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 gives one pair, such as (0, 3), (1, 5), and so on. That is 6 pairs.

questions.prompt: A function has domain {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2} and rule y = x². How many different numbers are in its range?
questions.hint: Square each value. Some give the same result.
questions.solution: (−2)² = 4, (−1)² = 1, 0² = 0, 1² = 1, 2² = 4. The range is {0, 1, 4}, which has 3 numbers.

questions.prompt: Domain {−1, 0, 1, 2} and rule y = 2x + 1. What is the range?
questions.hint: Plug in each x-value: double it, then add 1.

questions.prompt: Which situation is a function of the first quantity?
choices: Each student paired with each of their siblings
Each parent paired with their children
Each birthday paired with the students born that day
Each student paired with their date of birth
questions.hint: A function needs exactly one output for each input.
questions.solution: A student has one date of birth, so that is a function. A student can have several siblings, a parent several children, and one date several students. Those give more than one output.

questions.prompt: A function follows the rule y = 2x + 3 and includes the pairs (1, 5), (2, 7), (3, 9), and (k, 11). Find k.
questions.hint: Set 2k + 3 equal to 11.

questions.prompt: What are the domain and range of {(−2, 4), (0, 0), (2, 4)}?
questions.hint: Domain is x, range is y. List repeats once.
questions.solution: x-values: −2, 0, 2. y-values: 4, 0, 4, so the range lists 4 once: {0, 4}.

teach.title: Reading f(x)
text: f(x) is read 'f of x'. It is the output of the function f when the input is x. It does not mean f times x.
To find f(4), replace every x in the rule with 4 and simplify.

example.problem: If f(x) = 2x + 3, find f(4).
steps: f(4) = 11. The point (4, 11) is on the graph.

teach.title: Negative inputs and squares
text: Put a negative input in parentheses so the signs stay right.
In x², the square applies to the whole input: (−3)² = 9, not −9.

example.problem: If g(x) = x² − 4x, find g(−3).

questions.prompt: If f(x) = 3x + 2, find f(4).
questions.hint: Replace x with 4, then multiply before adding.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = 5 − 2x, find f(3).
questions.hint: Multiply 2 by 3 first, then subtract from 5.

questions.prompt: What does f(4) = 9 tell you?
choices: When the input is 9, the output is 4
When the input is 4, the output is 9
The function f has a slope of 9
questions.hint: The number inside the parentheses is the input.
questions.solution: f(4) = 9 means input 4 gives output 9. The point (4, 9) is on the graph.

questions.prompt: If g(x) = x² − 4x, find g(−2).
questions.hint: (−2)² is positive. Then −4 times −2 is also positive.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = 4x − 1, which is f(−2)?
questions.hint: 4 times −2 is −8. Then subtract 1.

questions.prompt: If h(x) = 2x² − x + 1, find h(−3).
questions.hint: Square −3 first, then double it. Careful with −(−3).

questions.prompt: If f(x) = x² + 1, find f(2) + f(−2).
questions.hint: Find each value separately, then add.

questions.prompt: If p(x) = −x² + 3x, find p(4).
questions.hint: −x² means the negative of (x squared). Find 4² first.

teach.title: Plugging in an expression
text: The input can be a letter or an expression. Replace every x with the whole expression, in parentheses.
Then simplify. Use the distributive property when needed.

example.problem: If f(x) = 2x + 3, find f(a + 1).

teach.title: Function of a function
text: In f(g(x)), work from the inside out. Find g first, then put that result into f.

example.problem: f(x) = x + 4 and g(x) = 2x. Find g(f(1)).

questions.prompt: If f(x) = 3x − 2, what is f(a + 1)?
questions.hint: Use parentheses: 3(a + 1) − 2.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = x², what is f(x + 2)?
questions.hint: Square the whole (x + 2). Remember (x + 2)² = (x + 2)(x + 2).

questions.prompt: f(x) = 2x − 1. The difference f(k) − f(k − 1) is a number. What is it?
questions.hint: Find f(k) and f(k − 1) separately. Distribute carefully in the second.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = 2x + 5, what is f(−x)?
questions.hint: Replace x with −x. Only the x term changes sign.
questions.solution: f(−x) = 2(−x) + 5 = −2x + 5. The +5 does not change.

questions.prompt: g(x) = x + 4 and h(x) = 2x. Find h(g(3)).
questions.hint: Work from the inside: g(3) first.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = x² − x, what is f(2a)?
questions.hint: (2a)² = 4a². The 2 gets squared too.

questions.prompt: f(x) = 3x + 1. Then f(x + h) − f(x) = kh for a number k. Find k.
questions.hint: Expand f(x + h) first. Then subtract f(x).
questions.solution: f(x + h) = 3(x + h) + 1 = 3x + 3h + 1. Subtract f(x) = 3x + 1: the result is 3h. So k = 3.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = x² + x, find f(3) − f(−3).
questions.hint: f(−3) = 9 + (−3). Evaluate each, then subtract.

teach.title: Solving f(x) = k
text: f(x) = k asks: which input x gives the output k? Set the rule equal to k and solve for x.
If x is squared, take the square root and remember both the positive and negative answers.

example.problem: If f(x) = 2x + 7, find x when f(x) = 15.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = 2x + 7 and f(x) = 21, find x.
questions.hint: Write 2x + 7 = 21 and undo the + 7 first.
questions.solution: 2x + 7 = 21. Subtract 7: 2x = 14. Divide by 2: x = 7.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = 5x − 3 and f(x) = 22, find x.
questions.hint: Add 3 to both sides first.
questions.solution: 5x − 3 = 22. Add 3: 5x = 25. Divide by 5: x = 5.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = −3x + 4 and f(x) = −11, find x.
questions.hint: Subtract 4, then divide by −3.
questions.solution: −3x + 4 = −11. Subtract 4: −3x = −15. Divide by −3: x = 5.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = x/2 + 1 and f(x) = 6, find x.
questions.hint: Subtract 1, then multiply both sides by 2.
questions.solution: x/2 + 1 = 6. Subtract 1: x/2 = 5. Multiply by 2: x = 10.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = x² and f(x) = 36, find every x that works.
questions.hint: Two numbers have a square of 36.
questions.solution: x² = 36. Take square roots: x = 6 or x = −6. Both give 36 when squared.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = x² − 5 and f(x) = 20, find every x that works.
questions.hint: Add 5 to both sides first. Then take the square root.
questions.solution: x² − 5 = 20. Add 5: x² = 25. So x = 5 or x = −5.

questions.prompt: f(x) = 4x − 9. Which equation do you solve to find a when f(a) = 3?
questions.hint: The output f(a) is 3. The input is the unknown a.
questions.solution: f(a) = 4a − 9. Setting the output equal to 3 gives 4a − 9 = 3. Solving: 4a = 12, a = 3.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = (2x − 1)/3 and f(x) = 5, find x.
questions.hint: Multiply both sides by 3 first.
questions.solution: (2x − 1)/3 = 5. Multiply by 3: 2x − 1 = 15. Add 1: 2x = 16. Divide by 2: x = 8. Check: (16 − 1)/3 = 5.

teach.title: Reading values from graphs and tables
text: To find f(a) on a graph, go to x = a and read the height of the curve. To solve f(x) = k, go to height k and read the x-value.
In a table, f(a) is the y-value in the column where x = a.

example.problem: Table: x = 0, 1, 2 and f(x) = 6, 4, 2. Find f(1) and solve f(x) = 2.
steps: f(1): the column with x = 1 has y = 4. So f(1) = 4.
f(x) = 2: the column with y = 2 has x = 2. So x = 2.

questions.prompt: Using the graph of f, find f(3).
questions.hint: Go to x = 3 on the horizontal axis, then up to the line.
questions.solution: At x = 3 the line is at height 5. So f(3) = 5.

questions.prompt: Using the same line, y = 2x − 1, for what x is f(x) = 3?
questions.hint: Start at height 3 on the vertical axis and go across to the line.
questions.solution: The line reaches height 3 at x = 2. Check: 2(2) − 1 = 3.

questions.hint: Find the column where x = 2.
questions.solution: The column with x = 2 has y = −5. So f(2) = −5.

questions.prompt: Same table: x = −1, 0, 1, 2 and f(x) = 4, 1, −2, −5. For what x is f(x) = −2?
questions.hint: Find −2 in the f(x) row, then look at its x.
questions.solution: The value −2 is in the column with x = 1. So x = 1.

questions.prompt: From the graph of f(x) = x² − 4, find every x for which f(x) = 0.
questions.hint: These are the x-values where the graph crosses the x-axis.
questions.solution: The curve crosses the x-axis at x = −2 and x = 2. Check: 2² − 4 = 0 and (−2)² − 4 = 0.

questions.prompt: Table: x = 0, 1, 2, 3 and f(x) = 3, 5, 7, 9. Which rule matches the table?
questions.hint: f(0) tells you the number added. Then see how much f grows each step.
questions.solution: f(0) = 3 so the constant is 3. The values go up by 2 each step, so the rule is f(x) = 2x + 3. Check f(3) = 9.

questions.prompt: f(x) = 2x + 3 and g(x) = x² − 1. Find f(g(2)).
questions.hint: Do g(2) first, then use that as the input to f.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = x² − 2x and f(x) = 3, find every x that works.
questions.hint: Set x² − 2x = 3, move everything to one side, and factor.
questions.solution: x² − 2x = 3, so x² − 2x − 3 = 0. Factor: (x − 3)(x + 1) = 0. So x = 3 or x = −1. Check: 9 − 6 = 3 and 1 + 2 = 3.

teach.title: Slope from two points
text: Slope measures steepness: rise over run. Given (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂), m = (y₂ − y₁) / (x₂ − x₁).
Subtract in the same order on top and bottom. Either point can go first.

example.problem: Find the slope through (1, 2) and (4, 11).

questions.prompt: Find the slope of the line through (1, 2) and (3, 8).
questions.hint: Subtract the y-values, then the x-values, in the same order.

questions.prompt: Find the slope of the line through (0, 5) and (4, 1).
questions.hint: The y-value goes down as x goes up.

questions.prompt: Find the slope of the line through (−2, 3) and (4, 6).
Find the slope of the line through (−3, −1) and (2, −11).
questions.hint: Be careful with the double negatives: −11 − (−1) and 2 − (−3).

questions.prompt: What is the slope through (2, 5) and (6, 1)?
questions.hint: Rise is 1 − 5. Run is 6 − 2.

questions.prompt: Find the slope of the line through (5, −2) and (−3, 4).
questions.hint: Use the same order for both: 4 − (−2) on top, −3 − 5 on the bottom.

questions.prompt: Find the slope of the line through (2, −3) and (7, 9). Give it as a fraction or decimal.
A student finds the slope through (4, 9) and (1, 3) as (9 − 3)/(1 − 4). What went wrong?
choices: They subtracted in opposite orders on top and bottom
They should have added the y-values
They should have used the x-values on top
questions.hint: On top they did point 1 minus point 2. On the bottom?
questions.solution: The top uses (4, 9) first, but the bottom starts with the x of (1, 3). The orders must match: (9 − 3)/(4 − 1) = 6/3 = 2. The student got −2.

teach.title: Slope from a graph or a table
text: On a graph, pick two clear points on the line. Count the rise (up is positive, down is negative) and the run (right is positive).
In a table, slope is the change in y divided by the change in x. If it is the same for every pair of rows, the relationship is linear.

example.problem: Table: x = 0, 2, 4 and y = 1, 7, 13. Find the slope.
steps: From x = 0 to x = 2: change in x is 2, change in y is 6.
Check the next pair: change in x is 2, change in y is 6. Same slope, so it is linear.

questions.prompt: What is the slope of the graphed line?
questions.hint: The line passes through (0, 1) and (1, 3). How far up per step right?
questions.solution: From (0, 1) to (1, 3): rise 2, run 1. Slope = 2.

questions.prompt: The graphed line goes down to the right. What is its slope?
questions.hint: The line goes down to the right. Use (0, 3) and (2, 2).
questions.solution: From (0, 3) to (2, 2): rise −1, run 2. Slope = −1/2.

questions.prompt: Table: x = 0, 2, 4, 6 and y = 1, 7, 13, 19. Find the slope.
questions.hint: Pick two rows. Change in y over change in x.
questions.solution: From (0, 1) to (2, 7): (7 − 1)/(2 − 0) = 3. The other rows also change by 6 in y per 2 in x, so the slope is 3.

questions.prompt: Table: x = −2, 1, 4 and y = 9, 3, −3. Find the slope.
questions.hint: x goes up 3 each time. How does y change?

questions.prompt: Table: x = 1, 2, 3, 4 and y = 2, 5, 9, 14. Is the rate of change constant?
choices: No, y changes by 3, then 4, then 5, so it is not linear
questions.hint: Find the change in y between each pair of rows. The x-values go up by 1 each time.
questions.solution: Changes in y: 5 − 2 = 3, 9 − 5 = 4, 14 − 9 = 5. The change is not constant, so the rate of change is not constant and the table is not linear.

questions.prompt: The graphed line passes through the origin. Which is its slope?
questions.hint: The line passes through (0, 0) and (3, 1). Rise over run.
questions.solution: From (0, 0) to (3, 1): rise 1, run 3. The line goes up to the right, so the slope is +1/3.

questions.prompt: Table: x = 3, 5, 9 and y = 4, 10, 22. Find the slope.
questions.hint: The x-values are not evenly spaced, so divide each time.

questions.prompt: Read two clear points from the graph. What is the slope of the line?
questions.hint: From (0, 4) to (1, 2), the line goes down.
questions.solution: From (0, 4) to (1, 2): rise −2, run 1. Slope = −2.

teach.title: Horizontal and vertical lines
text: A horizontal line (y = c) has rise 0, so its slope is 0.
A vertical line (x = c) has run 0. You cannot divide by zero, so its slope is undefined.

example.problem: Slope through (2, 5) and (2, 9).
steps: 4/0 is undefined. The line is vertical, x = 2.

teach.title: Rate of change in words
text: In a real situation the slope is a rate: change in the output per one unit of the input. Always include units, like miles per hour.
A negative rate means the quantity is decreasing.

example.problem: A candle is 20 cm at 1 hour and 14 cm at 4 hours. Find the rate.

questions.prompt: Find the slope of the line through (3, 5) and (9, 5).
questions.hint: The y-values match. What is the rise?
questions.solution: m = (5 − 5)/(9 − 3) = 0/6 = 0. It is a horizontal line.

questions.prompt: What is the slope of the line through (4, −2) and (4, 7)?
questions.hint: The x-values match. What is the run?
questions.solution: m = (7 − (−2))/(4 − 4) = 9/0. Dividing by zero is undefined. The line is vertical.

questions.prompt: What is the slope of the line y = 4?
questions.hint: y = 4 is a horizontal line.
questions.solution: y = 4 is horizontal at height 4. A flat line rises 0, so the slope is 0.

questions.prompt: What is the slope of the line x = −2?
questions.hint: x = −2 is a straight up-and-down line.
questions.solution: x = −2 is a vertical line. Its run is 0, so its slope is undefined. It is not 0 and it is not −2.

questions.prompt: A car travels 150 miles in 3 hours at a steady pace. What is the rate of change in miles per hour?
questions.hint: Change in distance over change in time.
questions.solution: 150 miles / 3 hours = 50 miles per hour.

questions.prompt: At 2 pm the temperature is 70°F. At 6 pm it is 58°F. What is the rate of change in degrees per hour?
questions.hint: The temperature went down. Divide the change by the number of hours.
questions.solution: Change in temperature: 58 − 70 = −12. Change in time: 6 − 2 = 4 hours. Rate = −12/4 = −3 degrees per hour.

questions.prompt: A plant is 12 cm tall at week 2 and 33 cm tall at week 5. How many cm per week does it grow?
questions.hint: Change in height over change in weeks.
questions.solution: Height change: 33 − 12 = 21 cm. Time: 5 − 2 = 3 weeks. Rate = 21/3 = 7 cm per week.

questions.prompt: A tank's water level has a slope of −3 gallons per minute. What does that mean?
choices: The tank gains 3 gallons every minute
The tank loses 3 gallons every minute
questions.hint: Negative means decreasing.
questions.solution: The slope is the change in water per minute. −3 means the water goes down by 3 gallons each minute.

teach.title: Using slope to find missing values
text: When a slope is given, set up (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁) = m with the unknown in it, then solve the equation.
Compare steepness by size: a slope of −5 is steeper than a slope of 3, because 5 > 3.

example.problem: The line through (1, 4) and (3, k) has slope 5. Find k.

questions.prompt: The line through (2, k) and (5, 10) has slope 3. Find k.
questions.hint: Write (10 − k)/(5 − 2) = 3 and solve.
questions.solution: (10 − k)/3 = 3. Multiply by 3: 10 − k = 9. So k = 1.

questions.prompt: The line through (1, 4) and (m, −2) has slope −2. Find m.
questions.solution: −6/(m − 1) = −2. Multiply by (m − 1): −6 = −2(m − 1). Divide by −2: 3 = m − 1, so m = 4.

questions.prompt: The line through (−3, y) and (1, 5) has slope 1/2. Find y.
questions.hint: Run is 1 − (−3) = 4. So rise must be half of the run.
questions.solution: (5 − y)/4 = 1/2. Multiply by 4: 5 − y = 2. So y = 3.

questions.prompt: Which pair of points gives a line with slope −2/3?
questions.hint: Find the slope for each pair. The sign matters.

questions.prompt: The points (0, −1), (2, 5), and (5, k) all lie on one line. Find k.
questions.hint: Find the slope from the first two points, then use it to reach x = 5.

questions.prompt: A ramp rises 2 feet over a horizontal distance of 24 feet. What is its slope?
questions.hint: Slope is rise over run.

questions.prompt: A company sold 120 items in month 1 and 300 items in month 4. How many more items per month is it selling, on average?
questions.hint: Change in items over change in months. Month 4 minus month 1 is 3 months.
questions.solution: Items: 300 − 120 = 180. Months: 4 − 1 = 3. Rate = 180/3 = 60 items per month.

questions.prompt: Which line is steepest: slope 3/4, −5/2, 2, or −1?
questions.hint: Steepness depends on the size of the slope, not its sign.
questions.solution: Compare 3/4, 5/2, 2, 1 as sizes. 5/2 = 2.5 is the largest, so the line with slope −5/2 is steepest.

teach.title: Slope-intercept form
text: y = mx + b. The slope is m. The y-intercept is b, where the line crosses the y-axis at (0, b).
If you know the slope and one point, plug them in to find b.

example.problem: Write the line with slope 3 through (2, 7).

teach.title: Rewriting into slope-intercept form
text: Solve for y. Do the same thing to every term, including dividing the whole right side.

example.problem: Put 2x + y = 5 in slope-intercept form.

questions.prompt: Which equation has slope 3 and y-intercept −2?
questions.hint: In y = mx + b, m is the slope and b is the y-intercept.
questions.solution: m = 3 and b = −2, so y = 3x − 2.

questions.prompt: What is the y-intercept of y = −4x + 9?
questions.hint: It is the constant, the number without x.
questions.solution: In y = mx + b, b = 9. The line crosses the y-axis at (0, 9).

questions.prompt: Which equation has slope −1/2 and y-intercept 4?
questions.hint: Slope goes with x. The y-intercept stands alone.

questions.prompt: A line with slope 3 passes through (2, 7). In y = 3x + b, what is b?
questions.hint: Substitute x = 2 and y = 7 and solve for b.

questions.prompt: A line with slope −2 passes through (−1, 3). In y = −2x + b, what is b?
questions.hint: −2 times −1 is positive.

questions.prompt: Which equation matches the graph?
questions.hint: Where does the line cross the y-axis? Then count rise over run.
questions.solution: It crosses the y-axis at (0, −3), so b = −3. From (0, −3) to (1, −1) is rise 2, run 1, so m = 2. y = 2x − 3.

questions.prompt: Rewrite 3x + y = 5 in slope-intercept form. What is the slope?
questions.hint: Subtract 3x from both sides to get y by itself.
questions.solution: y = −3x + 5. The slope is −3.

questions.prompt: Solve 2y = 6x − 4 for y.
questions.hint: Divide every term by 2, not just one.
questions.solution: Divide both sides by 2: y = 3x − 2.

teach.title: Point-slope form
text: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) is the line with slope m through the point (x₁, y₁).
The signs flip: the point (3, −2) puts x − 3 and y + 2 in the equation.

example.problem: Write the line with slope 4 through (3, −2).

questions.prompt: Which is the line with slope 4 through (3, −2) in point-slope form?
questions.hint: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁). Subtracting a negative gives a plus.

questions.prompt: The line y − 5 = −3(x + 1) has which slope and point?
questions.solution: y − 5 = −3(x − (−1)). So m = −3 and the point is (−1, 5).

questions.prompt: The line y − 1 = 2(x − 4) has y-intercept b. Find b.
questions.hint: Distribute 2, then add 1.
questions.solution: y − 1 = 2x − 8. So y = 2x − 7. The y-intercept is −7.

questions.prompt: A line goes through (1, 3) and (3, 9). Write it in point-slope form, then simplify to y = mx + b. What is b?
questions.hint: First find the slope, then use (1, 3).

questions.prompt: Which equation is the line through (−2, 5) and (2, −3) in point-slope form using (−2, 5)?
questions.hint: Find the slope: change in y over change in x.

questions.prompt: A line has slope −1/2 and passes through (4, 1). Find its y-intercept.
Find the x-intercept of y − 2 = 3(x − 1). Give a fraction or decimal.
questions.hint: Simplify to y = 3x − 1, then set y = 0.

questions.prompt: Which equation is the same line as y − 4 = 2(x − 3)?
questions.hint: Distribute 2 and then add 4 to both sides.

teach.title: Standard form and intercepts
text: Standard form is Ax + By = C. To find the x-intercept, set y = 0. To find the y-intercept, set x = 0.
Slope in standard form is −A/B.

example.problem: Find the intercepts of 2x + 3y = 12.
steps: Set y = 0: 2x = 12, so x = 6. The x-intercept is (6, 0).
Set x = 0: 3y = 12, so y = 4. The y-intercept is (0, 4).

questions.prompt: What is the x-intercept (the x-value) of 2x + 3y = 12?
questions.hint: Set y = 0.

questions.prompt: What is the y-intercept (the y-value) of 2x + 3y = 12?
questions.hint: Set x = 0.

questions.prompt: What is the x-intercept (the x-value) of 5x − 2y = 20?
questions.hint: Set y = 0 and divide.

questions.prompt: Write y = −2x + 5 in standard form Ax + By = C.
questions.hint: Add 2x to both sides.
questions.solution: Add 2x to both sides: 2x + y = 5.

questions.prompt: What is the y-intercept (the y-value) of 4x − y = 8?
questions.hint: Set x = 0 and watch the sign on y.

questions.prompt: What is the slope of 3x − 4y = 12?
questions.hint: Solve for y, or use −A/B.
questions.solution: −4y = −3x + 12. Divide by −4: y = 3/4x − 3. The slope is 3/4.

questions.prompt: A line has x-intercept 3 and y-intercept −6. What is its slope?
questions.hint: The intercepts are the points (3, 0) and (0, −6).

questions.prompt: Which equation has x-intercept (4, 0) and y-intercept (0, −3)?
questions.hint: Plug both points into each equation.
questions.solution: Check 3x − 4y = 12. At (4, 0): 12 − 0 = 12. At (0, −3): 0 + 12 = 12. Both work. The others fail one of the points.

teach.title: Writing from two points, a graph, or a story
text: With two points: find the slope, then use one point to find b (or write point-slope).
From a story: the rate per unit is the slope. The starting amount is the y-intercept.

example.problem: A gym charges a $20 signup fee plus $15 per month. Write the cost C after m months.
steps: The fee per month is the slope: 15.
The signup fee at month 0 is the y-intercept: 20.

questions.prompt: Which is the line through (1, 5) and (3, 11)?
questions.hint: Slope first. Then use (1, 5) to find b.

questions.prompt: A line goes through (2, −1) and (6, 7). What is its y-intercept?
questions.hint: The slope is 8/4. Then plug in (2, −1).

questions.prompt: Which equation describes the graphed line?
questions.hint: Read the y-intercept first. Then find rise over run.
questions.solution: The line crosses the y-axis at −2. From (0, −2) to (2, −1): rise 1, run 2, so m = 1/2. y = 1/2x − 2.

questions.prompt: A line goes through (−3, 4) and (3, −2). What is its y-intercept?
questions.hint: The slope is −6/6.

questions.prompt: A line passes through (0, 3) and (4, 11). What is y when x = 10?
questions.hint: Find the equation first: slope and y-intercept.

questions.prompt: A gym charges a $20 joining fee plus $15 per month. What is the total cost, in dollars, after 6 months?
questions.hint: Cost = 15 times months plus 20.

questions.prompt: A plumber charges a flat visit fee plus an hourly rate. A 3-hour job costs $135 and the visit fee is $45. What is the hourly rate in dollars?
questions.hint: Take away the visit fee, then divide by the hours.
questions.solution: 135 − 45 = 90 for labor. 90/3 = 30 dollars per hour.

questions.prompt: A plant is 7 cm tall after 2 weeks and 16 cm tall after 5 weeks. Which equation gives its height h after w weeks?
questions.hint: The growth rate is the slope. Plug in one data point to find b.

teach.title: Slopes of parallel and perpendicular lines
text: Parallel lines never meet. They have the same slope.
Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle. Their slopes are negative reciprocals: flip the fraction and change the sign. The product of the two slopes is −1.

example.problem: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to y = (2/3)x + 1.

questions.prompt: What is the slope of any line parallel to y = 4x − 1?
questions.hint: Parallel lines have equal slopes.
questions.solution: The slope of y = 4x − 1 is 4. A parallel line has the same slope, 4.

questions.prompt: What is the slope of any line perpendicular to y = 4x − 1? Give a fraction.
questions.hint: Flip 4 (think 4/1) and change the sign.
questions.solution: The slope is 4 = 4/1. Flip to 1/4 and change the sign: −1/4.

questions.prompt: A line has slope −2/3. What is the slope of a line perpendicular to it?
questions.hint: Flip the fraction, and change the sign from negative to positive.
questions.solution: Flip −2/3 to get 3/2 and change the sign: +3/2. Check: (−2/3)(3/2) = −1.

questions.prompt: Which pair of slopes belongs to perpendicular lines?
questions.hint: Multiply each pair. Perpendicular slopes multiply to −1.

questions.prompt: A line has slope 1/2. What is the slope of a perpendicular line?
questions.hint: Flip 1/2 and change the sign.
questions.solution: Flip 1/2 to 2/1 = 2. Change the sign: −2.

questions.prompt: What is the slope of a line perpendicular to y = −x + 7?
questions.hint: The slope of y = −x + 7 is −1.
questions.solution: The slope is −1 = −1/1. Flip: −1. Change the sign: 1.

questions.prompt: A line is horizontal. What is true about a line perpendicular to it?
choices: It is vertical, with an undefined slope
questions.hint: Picture the x-axis and a line crossing it at a right angle.
questions.solution: A horizontal line is perpendicular to a vertical line. Vertical lines have an undefined slope.

questions.prompt: A line with slope k is perpendicular to a line with slope 3/5. Find k.
questions.hint: k is the negative reciprocal of 3/5.

teach.title: Telling from equations
text: Get both equations to slope-intercept form, y = mx + b, and compare the slopes. Same slope with different b means parallel. Slopes with product −1 means perpendicular. Otherwise neither.
For standard form Ax + By = C, the slope is −A/B.

example.problem: Are 2x + y = 5 and y = (1/2)x − 3 parallel, perpendicular, or neither?

questions.prompt: y = 2x + 3 and y = 2x − 7 are...
questions.hint: Compare the slopes. Compare the y-intercepts too.
questions.solution: Both slopes are 2, and the y-intercepts 3 and −7 differ. So the lines are parallel.

questions.hint: Multiply the slopes.
questions.solution: 3 · (−1/3) = −1. The slopes are negative reciprocals, so the lines are perpendicular.

questions.prompt: 2x + y = 5 and 4x + 2y = 3 are...
questions.hint: Solve each for y. Compare the slope and the intercept.
questions.solution: 2x + y = 5 gives y = −2x + 5. 4x + 2y = 3 gives y = −2x + 3/2. Same slope −2, different intercepts: parallel.

questions.prompt: y = 2x + 1 and x + 2y = 6 are...
questions.hint: Solve the second equation for y.
questions.solution: x + 2y = 6 gives 2y = −x + 6, so y = −1/2x + 3. Slopes 2 and −1/2 multiply to −1: perpendicular.

questions.prompt: y = 3x + 2 and 3x + y = 5 are...
questions.hint: Rewrite 3x + y = 5 as y = ...
questions.solution: 3x + y = 5 gives y = −3x + 5. Slopes 3 and −3. They are not equal and 3 · (−3) = −9, not −1. So neither.

questions.prompt: y = kx + 3 is parallel to 2x − 3y = 6. Find k as a fraction.
questions.hint: Solve 2x − 3y = 6 for y to find its slope.
questions.solution: −3y = −2x + 6, so y = 2/3x − 2. The slope is 2/3. Parallel means k = 2/3.

questions.prompt: y = kx is perpendicular to y = (2/5)x − 1. Find k.
questions.hint: k is the negative reciprocal of 2/5.

questions.prompt: 6x − 2y = 8 and y = 3x − 5 are...
choices: Parallel but not the same line
questions.hint: Solve 6x − 2y = 8 for y and compare both slope and intercept.
questions.solution: −2y = −6x + 8, so y = 3x − 4. The other line is y = 3x − 5. Same slope 3, different intercepts: parallel and not the same line.

teach.title: Writing a line through a point
text: Step 1: get the slope you need (the same, or the negative reciprocal). Step 2: plug the point into y = mx + b to find b, or use y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).

example.problem: Write the line parallel to y = 2x + 5 through (1, 4).
steps: Parallel means slope 2. So y = 2x + b.

questions.prompt: Which line is parallel to y = 2x + 5 and goes through (3, 1)?
questions.hint: Use slope 2 and solve 1 = 2(3) + b.

questions.prompt: A line is perpendicular to y = 2x − 1 and goes through (4, 3). What is its y-intercept?
questions.hint: The new slope is −1/2. Then 3 = −1/2(4) + b.

questions.prompt: Which line is parallel to y = −3x + 1 and goes through (2, −4)?
questions.hint: Slope −3. Solve −4 = −3(2) + b.

questions.prompt: A line is parallel to y = 3x − 4 and goes through (−2, 1). What is its y-intercept?
questions.hint: 3 times −2 is −6.
questions.solution: The slope is 3. 1 = 3(−2) + b = −6 + b, so b = 7.

questions.prompt: Which line is perpendicular to y = (1/2)x + 3 and goes through (−1, 4)?
questions.hint: The new slope is −2. Solve 4 = −2(−1) + b.

questions.prompt: A line is parallel to 2x + y = 7 and goes through (3, 2). What is its y-intercept?
questions.hint: The slope of 2x + y = 7 is −2.
questions.solution: The slope is −2. 2 = −2(3) + b = −6 + b, so b = 8.

questions.prompt: A line is perpendicular to 4x + y = 3 and goes through (8, 5). What is its y-intercept?
questions.hint: 4x + y = 3 has slope −4. The perpendicular slope is 1/4.
questions.solution: The slope is 1/4. 5 = 1/4(8) + b = 2 + b, so b = 3.

questions.prompt: Which is the standard form of the line parallel to x − 2y = 4 through (2, 3)?
questions.hint: A parallel line keeps x − 2y and changes only the right side. Plug in (2, 3).
questions.solution: Parallel lines have the form x − 2y = C. At (2, 3): 2 − 6 = −4. So x − 2y = −4.

teach.title: Putting it together
text: A missing coordinate can be found by setting the slope between two points equal to the slope you need.
To test for a right angle in a shape, check whether two sides have slopes with product −1.

example.problem: Line through (0, 1) and (3, k) is parallel to y = 2x. Find k.

questions.prompt: A line passes through (1, 2) and (3, 8). What is the slope of a line perpendicular to it? Give a fraction.
questions.hint: Find its slope first, then take the negative reciprocal.
questions.solution: m = (8 − 2)/(3 − 1) = 3. The perpendicular slope is −1/3.

questions.prompt: Line A goes through (0, 1) and (2, 5). Line B goes through (1, 0) and (3, 4). How are they related?
questions.hint: Find each slope.
questions.solution: Line A: (5 − 1)/(2 − 0) = 2. Line B: (4 − 0)/(3 − 1) = 2. Same slope. Line A has y-intercept 1 and Line B passes through (1, 0), not on Line A, so they are different parallel lines.

questions.prompt: The line through (−1, 2) and (3, k) is perpendicular to y = −2x + 1. Find k.
questions.hint: The perpendicular slope is 1/2. Set (k − 2)/4 = 1/2.
questions.solution: The slope must be 1/2. (k − 2)/(3 − (−1)) = 1/2 gives (k − 2)/4 = 1/2. So k − 2 = 2 and k = 4.

questions.prompt: The line through (2, 1) and (m, 7) is parallel to y = 3x. Find m.
questions.hint: The slope must be 3: 6/(m − 2) = 3.

questions.prompt: A triangle has vertices A(1, 1), B(5, 3), and C(3, 7). At which vertex is there a right angle?
questions.hint: Find the slopes of AB, BC, and AC. Look for slopes that multiply to −1.
questions.solution: AB: (3 − 1)/(5 − 1) = 1/2. BC: (7 − 3)/(3 − 5) = −2. AC: (7 − 1)/(3 − 1) = 3. AB and BC: (1/2)(−2) = −1, so they are perpendicular. They meet at B.

questions.prompt: A line is perpendicular to y = −(2/3)x + 5 and goes through (6, −1). What is its y-intercept?
questions.hint: The new slope is 3/2. Then −1 = 3/2(6) + b.

questions.prompt: In a rectangle, one side has slope 5/3. What is the slope of a side that meets it at a corner? Give a fraction.
questions.hint: Adjacent sides of a rectangle are perpendicular.
questions.solution: Neighboring sides are perpendicular, so the slope is the negative reciprocal of 5/3, which is −3/5.

questions.prompt: Which is the equation of the line through (3, −2) that is parallel to the x-axis?
questions.hint: A line parallel to the x-axis is horizontal. What stays the same on it?
questions.solution: A horizontal line has the same y-value everywhere. It passes through (3, −2), so y = −2.

teach.title: Solid or dashed boundary
text: To graph an inequality, first graph its boundary line. Treat the inequality sign as an equals sign.
If the sign is ≤ or ≥, the points on the line are solutions, so draw a solid line.
If the sign is < or >, the points on the line are not solutions, so draw a dashed line.

example.problem: Is the boundary of y > 2x + 1 solid or dashed?
steps: The sign is >, with no "or equal to" part.
So points on the line do not count. The line is dashed.

teach.title: Which side to shade
text: When y is alone on the left, y > shades above the line and y < shades below it.
With ≥ or ≤ the shading is the same, but the line is solid.

example.problem: Describe the graph of y ≤ −x + 4.
steps: The sign is ≤, so the boundary y = −x + 4 is solid.
y is less than the line, so shade below it.

questions.prompt: Which describes the graph of y > 3x − 2?
questions.hint: The sign is >. Does it include "equal to"? And y is greater than the line.
questions.solution: The sign is >, so the line is dashed. y is greater than the line, so shade above.

questions.prompt: Which describes the graph of y ≤ −x + 4?
questions.hint: The sign is ≤, which includes "equal to".
questions.solution: The sign is ≤, so the line is solid. y is less than the line, so shade below.

questions.prompt: What is the y-intercept of the boundary line of y ≥ 2x − 5?
questions.hint: The boundary line is y = 2x − 5. Find the b in y = mx + b.
questions.solution: The boundary is y = 2x − 5. The y-intercept is −5.

questions.prompt: What is the slope of the boundary line of y < −(3/4)x + 2?
questions.hint: Ignore the < and read the slope from y = mx + b.
questions.solution: The boundary is y = −(3/4)x + 2. The slope is −3/4.

questions.prompt: Which inequality has a dashed boundary line?
questions.hint: Dashed lines go with < and > only.
questions.solution: Only < and > give a dashed line. The others have ≤ or ≥, so they are solid. The answer is y < 3x − 1.

questions.prompt: A point on the boundary line of y > 5x + 3 has x = 2. What is its y-coordinate?
questions.hint: Put x = 2 into the boundary line y = 5x + 3.

questions.prompt: What is the boundary line of 2x + y ≥ 6?
questions.hint: Change the inequality sign to an equals sign. Do not move anything else.
questions.solution: The boundary line uses = in place of ≥, so it is 2x + y = 6.

questions.prompt: The line y = 2x − 1 is drawn. The graph is solid with shading above it. Which inequality is it?
questions.hint: Solid means the sign has an "or equal to". Above means y is greater.
questions.solution: Solid means ≥ or ≤. Shading above means y is greater than the line. So y ≥ 2x − 1.

teach.title: Is a point a solution?
text: A point (x, y) is a solution if the inequality is true when you put in its x and y.
Put the numbers in, then check whether the statement is true or false. For ≤ and ≥, "equal" counts as true.

example.problem: Is (1, 4) a solution of y > 2x + 1?
steps: 4 > 3 is true. So (1, 4) is a solution.

teach.title: Test point for shading
text: Pick a test point that is not on the line. (0, 0) is easiest.
If it makes the inequality true, shade the side with that point. If false, shade the other side.

example.problem: Which side of the line do you shade for y < 2x − 3?
steps: So shade the side that does not contain (0, 0).

questions.prompt: Is (1, 4) a solution of y > 2x + 1?
choices: No, because the line is dashed
questions.hint: Put x = 1 and y = 4 in. Is the statement true?
questions.solution: 4 > 2(1) + 1 means 4 > 3. That is true, so yes.

questions.prompt: Is (−2, 3) a solution of y ≤ −x + 1?
choices: No, because the point is on the line
questions.hint: Work out −(−2) + 1 first. With ≤, equal counts.
questions.solution: −(−2) + 1 = 3. The test is 3 ≤ 3, which is true. The point is on a solid line, so it counts.

questions.prompt: Look at y > 3x − 4. For the point (2, k), what is the largest whole number k that is NOT a solution?
questions.hint: Find 3(2) − 4. Then ask which k are not greater than that.
questions.solution: 3(2) − 4 = 2. The point is a solution when k > 2. So k = 2 is not a solution, and 2 is the largest whole number that is not.

questions.prompt: Is (3, −1) a solution of 2x + 3y < 4?
questions.solution: 2(3) + 3(−1) = 6 − 3 = 3. Then 3 < 4 is true, so yes.

questions.prompt: How many of the points (0, 0), (1, 5), (−2, −1), (3, 3) are solutions of y ≥ x + 1?
questions.hint: Test each point. Equal counts because of ≥.
questions.solution: (0, 0): 0 ≥ 1 is false. (1, 5): 5 ≥ 2 is true. (−2, −1): −1 ≥ −1 is true. (3, 3): 3 ≥ 4 is false. Two points work.

questions.prompt: To graph y < 2x − 3, you test (0, 0) and get 0 < −3, which is false. What do you shade?
choices: The side that does not contain (0, 0)
questions.hint: A false test point means (0, 0) is not in the solution.
questions.solution: False means (0, 0) is not a solution. Shade the other side. (Here that is below the line, as y < says.)

questions.prompt: The point (a, 7) is on the boundary line of y ≥ 2x + 1. Find a.
questions.hint: Put y = 7 into y = 2x + 1.
questions.solution: 7 = 2a + 1, so 2a = 6 and a = 3.

questions.prompt: Which point is a solution of 3x − y ≤ 2?
questions.hint: Work out 3x − y for each point. You need a value of 2 or less.

teach.title: Get y alone
text: To read an inequality like a line, solve it for y. Keep the sign the same while you add and subtract.
If you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number, flip the inequality sign.

example.problem: Solve x − 2y < 6 for y.
steps: Divide by −2. The sign flips: y > (1/2)x − 3.
So the boundary is dashed with shading above.

questions.prompt: Solve 2x + y ≥ 5 for y.
questions.hint: Subtract 2x from both sides. No flip is needed.
questions.solution: Subtract 2x: y ≥ −2x + 5. You did not divide by a negative, so the sign stays.

questions.prompt: Solve x − 2y < 6 for y.
questions.hint: After subtracting x you divide by −2. What happens to the sign?
questions.solution: −2y < −x + 6. Divide by −2 and flip: y > (1/2)x − 3.

questions.prompt: What is the slope of the boundary line of 4x − 2y ≥ 8?
questions.hint: Solve for y first, then read the slope. Dividing by −2 flips the sign but does not change the slope rule.
questions.solution: −2y ≥ −4x + 8, so y ≤ 2x − 4. The slope is 2.

questions.prompt: What is the y-intercept of the boundary line of 3x + 4y ≤ 12?
questions.hint: For the intercept, put x = 0 into the boundary 3x + 4y = 12.
questions.solution: With x = 0: 4y = 12, so y = 3.

questions.prompt: Solve 3y − 6x > 9 for y.
questions.hint: Add 6x first, then divide by 3. Positive 3, so no flip.
questions.solution: 3y > 6x + 9. Divide by 3: y > 2x + 3.

questions.prompt: Which is the same as −y > 2x − 1?
questions.hint: Multiply both sides by −1, and flip the sign.
questions.solution: Multiply by −1: y < −2x + 1. Every sign changes and the inequality flips.

questions.prompt: The boundary line of −3y ≤ 6x + 12 crosses the y-axis where? Give the y-value.
questions.hint: Put x = 0 in, then divide by −3.
questions.solution: With x = 0: −3y = 12, so y = −4. (The sign only flips for the inequality, not for the boundary line.)

questions.prompt: The line y = −(1/2)x + 3 is drawn. The graph is solid, shaded below. Which inequality is it?
questions.hint: Solid means a sign with "or equal to". Below means y is less.
questions.solution: Solid is ≤ or ≥. Shaded below means y is less than the line. So y ≤ −(1/2)x + 3.

teach.title: Writing an inequality from a graph
text: Find the boundary line: its slope and y-intercept. Then decide the sign.
Solid line: ≤ or ≥. Dashed line: < or >. Shaded above: > or ≥. Shaded below: < or ≤.
A vertical line x = a is shaded right for x > a (or ≥) and left for x < a (or ≤).

example.problem: A solid line passes through (0, 2) and (4, 0). The side with (3, 3) is shaded. Write the inequality.
steps: Slope: (0 − 2)/(4 − 0) = −1/2. The y-intercept is 2. Boundary: y = −(1/2)x + 2.
At x = 3 the line is at y = 0.5. The point (3, 3) is above it, so shade above.

questions.prompt: A solid boundary line passes through (0, 4) and (2, 0). The side with the origin is shaded. Which inequality is it?
questions.hint: Find the slope first. Then test the origin: is (0, 0) above or below the line?
questions.solution: Slope = (0 − 4)/(2 − 0) = −2, so the line is y = −2x + 4. At x = 0 the line is at 4, and the origin is below it. Solid and below: y ≤ −2x + 4.

questions.prompt: A boundary line passes through (0, −1) and (3, 5). What is its slope?
questions.hint: Use rise over run: (5 − (−1)) / (3 − 0).

questions.prompt: A solid line passes through (0, 2) and (4, 0). The side with (3, 3) is shaded. Which inequality is it?
questions.hint: Find the line first. Then check whether (3, 3) is above or below it.
questions.solution: The slope is −1/2, so the line is y = −(1/2)x + 2. At x = 3 the line is at 0.5, so (3, 3) is above. Solid and above: y ≥ −(1/2)x + 2.

questions.prompt: You have $30 for movies at $6 each and snacks at $3 each, so 6m + 3s ≤ 30. If m = 4, what is the greatest whole number of snacks s?
questions.hint: Put m = 4 into 6m + 3s ≤ 30 and solve for s.
questions.solution: 24 + 3s ≤ 30, so 3s ≤ 6 and s ≤ 2. The most is 2 snacks.

questions.prompt: Which point is a solution of 6m + 3s ≤ 30?
questions.hint: Work out 6m + 3s for each pair. It must be 30 or less.

questions.prompt: The boundary of 5x − 2y ≥ 4 has y = 3 at one point. What is x?
questions.hint: Put y = 3 into 5x − 2y = 4.

questions.prompt: Which describes the graph of x > −2?
choices: Solid vertical line at x = −2, shade right
Dashed vertical line at x = −2, shade left
Dashed vertical line at x = −2, shade right
Dashed horizontal line at y = −2, shade above
questions.hint: x = −2 is a vertical line. Greater x means further right.
questions.solution: x = −2 is a vertical line. The sign > means dashed. Larger x is to the right, so shade right.

questions.prompt: How many points (x, y) with positive whole-number coordinates satisfy y < −x + 6?
questions.hint: This is x + y < 6, so x + y can be 2, 3, 4, or 5. Count the pairs for each.
questions.solution: x + y < 6 with x, y ≥ 1. Sum 2: 1 pair. Sum 3: 2. Sum 4: 3. Sum 5: 4. Total 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10.

teach.title: What a solution means
text: A system is two or more equations. The solution is a point that makes every equation true.
On a graph, it is where the lines cross. To check a point, put its x and y into each equation.

example.problem: Is (2, 3) a solution of y = x + 1 and y = −x + 5?
steps: It works in both, so (2, 3) is a solution.

questions.prompt: Is (2, 3) a solution of y = x + 1 and y = −x + 5?
choices: No, it fails the first equation
Yes, it works in both equations
No, it fails the second equation
Yes, because it works in the first equation
questions.hint: Check the point in each equation. It must work in both.
questions.solution: First: 3 = 2 + 1 is true. Second: 3 = −2 + 5 is true. So yes.

questions.prompt: Is (1, 4) a solution of y = 2x + 2 and y = −x + 3?
choices: No, it works only in the first equation
No, it works only in the second equation
Yes, because the x-values are small
questions.hint: Check the point in each equation separately.
questions.solution: First: 4 = 2(1) + 2 = 4, true. Second: 4 = −1 + 3 = 2, false. It fails the second equation, so it is not a solution.

questions.prompt: The line y = x + 2 is drawn. A second line is y = −x + 4. At the point where they cross, what is x?
questions.hint: At the crossing, both y-values are the same. Set x + 2 equal to −x + 4.
questions.solution: x + 2 = −x + 4, so 2x = 2 and x = 1.

questions.prompt: The lines y = 2x − 1 and y = x + 2 cross. What is the y-coordinate of the crossing point?
questions.hint: Find x first by setting 2x − 1 = x + 2. Then use either line.
questions.solution: 2x − 1 = x + 2 gives x = 3. Then y = 3 + 2 = 5.

questions.prompt: The line y = −x + 6 is drawn. A second line is y = x. Where do they cross?
questions.hint: Set −x + 6 equal to x.
questions.solution: −x + 6 = x, so x = 3 and y = 3. The crossing point is (3, 3).

questions.prompt: Which system has (−1, 2) as its solution?
questions.hint: Put x = −1 and y = 2 into both equations of each system.
questions.solution: For y = x + 3: −1 + 3 = 2, true. For y = −x + 1: 1 + 1 = 2, true. The other systems fail an equation.

questions.prompt: The lines y = 3x − 4 and y = −x + 8 cross at x = 3. What is y?
questions.hint: Put x = 3 into either line.

questions.prompt: For what value of k is (4, −1) a solution of x + ky = 5?
questions.hint: Put x = 4 and y = −1 in, then solve for k.

teach.title: Substitution
text: If one equation says y = (an expression), put that expression in place of y in the other equation.
Solve for x. Then use x to find y.

example.problem: Solve y = 2x and x + y = 12.

questions.prompt: Solve y = 2x and x + y = 12. What is x?
questions.hint: Put 2x in place of y in the second equation.
questions.solution: x + 2x = 12, so 3x = 12 and x = 4.

questions.prompt: Solve y = x + 4 and 2x + y = 13. What is x?
questions.hint: Replace y with x + 4 in the second equation.

questions.prompt: Solve y = 3x − 2 and y = x + 6. What is y?
questions.hint: Both expressions equal y, so set them equal. Then find y.
questions.solution: 3x − 2 = x + 6, so 2x = 8 and x = 4. Then y = 4 + 6 = 10.

questions.prompt: Solve y = x − 1 and 3x + y = 11. Which is the solution?
questions.hint: Replace y with x − 1, find x, then find y.
questions.solution: 3x + (x − 1) = 11, so 4x = 12 and x = 3. Then y = 3 − 1 = 2. The answer is (3, 2).

questions.prompt: Solve x = 2y + 1 and 3x − y = 8. What is y?
questions.hint: This time x is alone. Replace x with 2y + 1.
questions.solution: 3(2y + 1) − y = 8, so 6y + 3 − y = 8. That is 5y = 5, so y = 1.

questions.prompt: To solve y = 4x − 3 and 2x + 3y = 11, what is the correct first substitution?
questions.hint: Replace y by the whole expression, in brackets.
questions.solution: Replace y with (4x − 3) and keep the 3 in front: 2x + 3(4x − 3) = 11.

questions.prompt: Solve x − y = 2 and y = 3x − 10. What is x?
questions.hint: Replace y with 3x − 10. Watch the minus sign in front of y.

questions.prompt: One number is 3 more than twice another. Their sum is 21. What is the smaller number?
questions.hint: Let the smaller be b, so the other is 2b + 3. Their sum is 21.
questions.solution: b + (2b + 3) = 21, so 3b = 18 and b = 6. The other is 15.

teach.title: Solve for a variable first
text: If neither equation has y or x alone, pick a variable with a coefficient of 1 and solve for it.
Then substitute into the other equation. Put the whole expression in brackets.

example.problem: Solve x + y = 10 and 3x − y = 14.
steps: Solve the first for x: x = 10 − y.

questions.prompt: In 3x + 4y = 10 and x − 5y = 2, which is easiest to solve for a variable without fractions?
questions.hint: Look for a coefficient of 1 or −1.
questions.solution: x − 5y = 2 has an x with coefficient 1, so x = 5y + 2 has no fractions.

questions.prompt: Solve x + y = 10 and 3x − y = 14. What is x?
questions.hint: Solve the first for x: x = 10 − y. Substitute.
questions.solution: 3(10 − y) − y = 14 gives 30 − 4y = 14, so y = 4. Then x = 6.

questions.prompt: Solve x − 2y = 4 and 3x + 2y = 20. What is y?
questions.hint: Solve the first for x: x = 2y + 4.

questions.prompt: Solve 3x − y = 5 and x + 2y = 4. Which is the solution?
questions.hint: Solve the first for y: y = 3x − 5.
questions.solution: y = 3x − 5. Then x + 2(3x − 5) = 4, so 7x = 14 and x = 2. Then y = 1.

questions.prompt: Solve 2x + y = 1 and 4x + 3y = 5. What is y?
questions.hint: Solve the first for y: y = 1 − 2x.

questions.prompt: Substitute y = 5 − 2x into 3x − 2y = 4. Which equation do you get?
questions.hint: Use brackets so the −2 multiplies the whole expression.
questions.solution: Replace y with (5 − 2x): 3x − 2(5 − 2x) = 4.

questions.prompt: Solve x + 2y = 3 and 2x + 3y = 4. What is x?
questions.hint: Solve the first for x: x = 3 − 2y.

questions.prompt: A notebook costs $2 more than a pen. 3 notebooks and 2 pens cost $21. What does a pen cost, in dollars?
questions.hint: Let a pen cost p. A notebook costs p + 2.
questions.solution: 3(p + 2) + 2p = 21, so 5p + 6 = 21 and p = 3. A pen costs $3 (a notebook costs $5).

teach.title: No solution and infinitely many
text: If substituting leaves a false statement like 8 = 3, there is no solution. The lines are parallel.
If it leaves a true statement like 5 = 5, there are infinitely many solutions. The lines are the same line.
Lines with the same slope and different intercepts never meet.

example.problem: Solve y = 2x + 3 and y = 2x − 1.
steps: No solution. The lines are parallel.

questions.prompt: How many solutions do y = 2x + 3 and y = 2x − 1 have?
questions.hint: Compare the slopes and the y-intercepts.
questions.solution: The slopes are both 2 but the intercepts differ. The lines are parallel, so there is no solution.

questions.prompt: Substitute y = 3x − 4 into 6x − 2y = 8. What do you find?
choices: It gives x = 8, so one solution
It gives 8 = 8, so infinitely many solutions
questions.hint: Distribute the −2 and combine like terms.
questions.solution: 6x − 2(3x − 4) = 8 gives 6x − 6x + 8 = 8, so 8 = 8. Always true, so infinitely many solutions.

questions.prompt: For y = 4x + 1 and y = 4x + k, what value of k gives infinitely many solutions?
questions.hint: The two equations must describe the same line.
questions.solution: The slopes already match. The intercepts must match too, so k = 1.

questions.prompt: Substitute y = −x + 5 into 2x + 2y = 7. What do you find?
choices: It gives 10 = 10, so infinitely many solutions
It gives x = 3, so one solution
questions.hint: Distribute the 2 and see whether the x terms cancel.
questions.solution: 2x + 2(−x + 5) = 7 gives 2x − 2x + 10 = 7, so 10 = 7. False, so no solution.

questions.prompt: For y = 5x − 2 and y = kx + 7 to have no solution, what must k be?
questions.hint: No solution means parallel lines with different intercepts.
questions.solution: Parallel lines have the same slope, so k = 5. The intercepts −2 and 7 differ, so they never meet.

questions.prompt: Solve y = x − 3 and 2x + y = 12. What is y?
questions.hint: Replace y with x − 3 in the second equation.

questions.prompt: The line y = 2x + 1 is drawn. A second line has slope 2 and y-intercept 4. How many solutions does the system have?
questions.hint: Same slope, different intercept: what does that mean for the lines?
questions.solution: Both lines have slope 2 but different intercepts (1 and 4). They are parallel, so the system has no solution.

questions.prompt: Hannah saves y = 20 + 5x dollars after x weeks. Ben saves y = 5 + 8x. After how many weeks do they have the same amount?
questions.hint: Set the two expressions equal.
questions.solution: 20 + 5x = 5 + 8x, so 15 = 3x and x = 5. After 5 weeks each has $45.

teach.title: Add or subtract
text: Line up the equations so the x terms, y terms, and numbers are in columns.
If one variable has opposite coefficients (like +y and −y), add the equations. If it has the same coefficient, subtract.
Solve for the leftover variable, then put it back to find the other.

example.problem: Solve x + y = 11 and x − y = 3.
steps: The y terms are +y and −y, so add: 2x = 14.
Then 7 + y = 11, so y = 4. The solution is (7, 4).

questions.prompt: Solve x + y = 11 and x − y = 3. What is x?
questions.hint: The y terms are opposites. Add the equations.
questions.solution: 2x = 14, so x = 7. (Then y = 4.)

questions.prompt: Solve 3x + y = 14 and 3x − y = 10. What is y?
questions.hint: Add to find x first, then put it back.
questions.solution: Add: 6x = 24, so x = 4. Then 12 + y = 14, so y = 2.

questions.prompt: To eliminate y from 4x + 3y = 17 and 2x + 3y = 11, what should you do?
choices: Subtract the second equation from the first
Subtract, to cancel the x terms
Add, to cancel the x terms
questions.hint: Both y terms are +3y. What cancels same terms?
questions.solution: The y coefficients are equal (+3y and +3y), so subtract. This leaves 2x = 6.

questions.prompt: Solve x + 2y = 9 and x − 2y = −1. What is y?
questions.hint: Add to get x. Then put x back in.
questions.solution: Add: 2x = 8, so x = 4. Then 4 + 2y = 9, so 2y = 5 and y = 5/2.

questions.prompt: Solve 5x + 2y = 16 and 3x + 2y = 8. What is y?
questions.hint: Both have +2y. Subtract the equations.
questions.solution: Subtract: 2x = 8, so x = 4. Then 20 + 2y = 16, so y = −2.

questions.prompt: Solve 2x + y = 7 and 4x − y = 5. Which is the solution?
questions.hint: The y terms are opposites. Add.
questions.solution: Add: 6x = 12, so x = 2. Then 4 + y = 7, so y = 3. The solution is (2, 3).

questions.prompt: Two numbers add to 25 and differ by 7. What is the larger number?
questions.hint: Write x + y = 25 and x − y = 7, then add.
questions.solution: Add: 2x = 32, so x = 16. The other number is 9.

questions.prompt: Solve 3x − 4y = 1 and 5x + 4y = 23. What is x?
questions.hint: The y terms are −4y and +4y. Add.
questions.solution: Add: 8x = 24, so x = 3. (Then y = 2.)

teach.title: Multiply one equation
text: If no variable cancels yet, multiply one whole equation so that one variable has opposite coefficients.
Multiply every term, including the number on the right.

example.problem: Solve 3x + 2y = 13 and x − y = 1.

questions.prompt: To eliminate y from 3x + 2y = 13 and x − y = 1, what is the best step?
choices: Multiply x − y = 1 by 2, then add
Multiply x − y = 1 by 3, then add
Multiply x − y = 1 by −2, then add
questions.hint: You need +2y and −2y.
questions.solution: Multiplying x − y = 1 by 2 gives 2x − 2y = 2. Now the y terms are +2y and −2y, so add.

questions.prompt: Solve 3x + 2y = 13 and x − y = 1. What is x?
questions.hint: Multiply the second equation by 2 and add.
questions.solution: 2x − 2y = 2. Add: 5x = 15, so x = 3. (Then y = 2.)

questions.prompt: Solve 2x + y = 10 and 3x + 2y = 17. What is y?
questions.hint: Multiply the first equation by −2 to cancel y.

questions.prompt: Solve 3x − y = 3 and 5x + 2y = 16. What is y?
questions.hint: Multiply the first equation by 2.
questions.solution: 6x − 2y = 6. Add to 5x + 2y = 16: 11x = 22, so x = 2. Then 6 − y = 3, so y = 3.

questions.prompt: Solve x + 3y = 5 and 3x + 2y = 1. Which is the solution?
questions.hint: Multiply the first equation by −3 to cancel x.

questions.prompt: Solve 4x − y = 9 and 2x + 3y = 1. What is x?
questions.hint: Multiply the first equation by 3 to cancel y.

questions.prompt: 3 muffins and 2 coffees cost $13. 1 muffin and 1 coffee cost $5. What does a coffee cost, in dollars?
questions.hint: Write 3m + 2c = 13 and m + c = 5. Multiply the second by 3 and subtract, or by −3 and add.
questions.solution: 3m + 3c = 15. Subtract 3m + 2c = 13: c = 2. A coffee costs $2.

questions.prompt: What do you get when you multiply every term of x − y = 4 by 3?
questions.hint: Multiply each term, including the 4.

teach.title: Multiply both equations
text: Sometimes you must multiply both equations. Choose a variable to cancel, then find a common multiple of its coefficients.
Make one coefficient positive and the other negative so that you can add.

example.problem: Solve 3x + 4y = 8 and 2x + 5y = 3.
steps: Cancel x. Multiply the first by 2 and the second by −3: 6x + 8y = 16 and −6x − 15y = −9.
Then 3x − 4 = 8, so x = 4. The solution is (4, −1).

questions.prompt: To eliminate x from 2x + 3y = 7 and 3x + 5y = 11 by adding, what should you do?
choices: Multiply the first by 3 and the second by 2
Multiply the first by 3 and the second by −2
Multiply the first by 5 and the second by 3
questions.hint: You need +6x and −6x.
questions.solution: 3 × first gives 6x + 9y = 21. −2 × second gives −6x − 10y = −22. The x terms cancel when added.

questions.prompt: Solve 3x + 4y = 8 and 2x + 5y = 3. What is y?
questions.hint: Multiply the first by 2 and the second by −3.

questions.prompt: Solve 5x + 2y = 1 and 3x − 5y = 13. What is x?
questions.hint: To cancel y, multiply the first by 5 and the second by 2.

questions.prompt: Solve 2x + 3y = 16 and 5x − 2y = 21. What is y?
questions.hint: To cancel y, multiply the first by 2 and the second by 3.

questions.prompt: Solve 3x − 2y = 8 and 2x + 5y = −1. Which is the solution?
questions.hint: To cancel y, multiply the first by 5 and the second by 2.

questions.prompt: Solve 6x + 5y = 3 and 4x − 3y = 21. What is y?
questions.hint: To cancel y, multiply the first by 3 and the second by 5.

questions.prompt: 2 sandwiches and 3 drinks cost $19. 3 sandwiches and 2 drinks cost $21. What does a sandwich cost, in dollars?
questions.hint: Write 2s + 3d = 19 and 3s + 2d = 21. Multiply to make the s terms match.
questions.solution: 3 × first: 6s + 9d = 57. 2 × second: 6s + 4d = 42. Subtract: 5d = 15, so d = 3. Then 2s + 9 = 19, so s = 5.

questions.prompt: You multiply 4x + 3y = 6 by 2 and 5x − 2y = 19 by 3. What is the correct next step?
questions.hint: Write both new equations first. The y terms should be +6y and −6y.
questions.solution: 8x + 6y = 12 and 15x − 6y = 57. The y terms are opposites, so add: 23x = 69.

teach.title: Special cases and rearranging
text: First put both equations in the form Ax + By = C. Then eliminate.
If everything cancels and you get a false statement like 0 = −3, there is no solution.
If you get a true statement like 0 = 0, there are infinitely many solutions.

example.problem: Solve 3x − y = 4 and 6x − 2y = 5.
steps: That is false, so there is no solution.

questions.prompt: Solve 2x + 4y = 6 and x + 2y = 3. What happens?
questions.hint: Multiply the second equation by −2 and add.
questions.solution: −2x − 4y = −6. Add to 2x + 4y = 6: 0 = 0. That is true, so there are infinitely many solutions.

questions.prompt: Solve 3x − y = 4 and 6x − 2y = 5. What happens?
questions.hint: Multiply the first equation by −2 and add.
questions.solution: −6x + 2y = −8. Add to 6x − 2y = 5: 0 = −3. False, so no solution.

questions.prompt: Solve y = 2x − 5 and 3x + y = 5. What is y?
questions.hint: Rewrite the first as −2x + y = −5. Then subtract or substitute.
questions.solution: Subtract (−2x + y = −5) from (3x + y = 5): 5x = 10, so x = 2. Then y = 2(2) − 5 = −1.

questions.prompt: For 2x + 3y = 5 and 4x + 6y = k, what k gives infinitely many solutions?
questions.hint: The second equation must be a multiple of the first.
questions.solution: Multiply the first by 2: 4x + 6y = 10. So k = 10.

questions.prompt: Solve 2x + 5y = 11 and 4x − 3y = −17. What is x?
questions.hint: Multiply the first equation by −2 to cancel x.

questions.prompt: Solve 5x + 2y = 4 and 3x + 2y = 0. Which is the solution?
questions.hint: Both have +2y. Subtract.
questions.solution: Subtract: 2x = 4, so x = 2. Then 6 + 2y = 0, so y = −3. The solution is (2, −3).

questions.prompt: Twice the first number plus the second is 17. The first minus the second is 1. What is the first number?
questions.hint: Write 2a + b = 17 and a − b = 1. Add.
questions.solution: Add: 3a = 18, so a = 6. Then b = 5.

questions.prompt: The solution of x + y = 7 and x − y = k has x = 5. What is k?
questions.hint: Find y from the first equation, then find k.
questions.solution: x + y = 7 gives y = 2. Then k = 5 − 2 = 3.

levels.title: System word problems and systems of inequalities

teach.title: Write the system
text: Choose a variable for each unknown. Write one equation for the counts and one equation for the money (or value).
Solve with substitution or elimination. Then answer the question that was asked.

example.problem: Tickets cost $9 for adults and $5 for students. 80 tickets sold for $520. How many adult tickets?
steps: Let a = adults and s = students. a + s = 80 and 9a + 5s = 520.

questions.prompt: Adult tickets cost $9 and student tickets cost $5. 80 tickets sold for $520. Which system fits (a = adults, s = students)?
questions.hint: One equation counts tickets. The other adds up the money.
questions.solution: Number of tickets: a + s = 80. Money: 9a + 5s = 520.

questions.prompt: Solve a + s = 80 and 9a + 5s = 520. How many adult tickets were sold?
questions.hint: Replace s with 80 − a in the money equation.

questions.prompt: A jar has 15 coins, all nickels and dimes, worth 115 cents. How many dimes?
questions.hint: Let n = nickels and d = dimes. n + d = 15 and 5n + 10d = 115.

questions.prompt: Two numbers add to 30. One is 4 more than the other. Which system fits?
questions.hint: "4 more than" means add 4.
questions.solution: Sum: x + y = 30. "4 more than the other": x = y + 4.

questions.prompt: Two numbers add to 30. One is 4 more than the other. What is the larger number?
questions.hint: Replace x with y + 4 in x + y = 30.

questions.prompt: Plan A costs $20 to join plus $10 a month. Plan B has no joining fee and costs $15 a month. After how many months do the plans cost the same?
questions.hint: Write each total cost and set them equal.
questions.solution: 20 + 10m = 15m, so 20 = 5m and m = 4. Both cost $60.

questions.prompt: Pens cost $2 and notebooks cost $3. Maria buys 12 items for $31. Which purchase did she make?
questions.hint: Check each choice: the count must be 12 and the cost $31.
questions.solution: 5 pens + 7 notebooks: 5 + 7 = 12 and 10 + 21 = 31. The others give $29, $30, and $32.

questions.prompt: A shop sells hats for $12 and scarves for $8. It sold 25 items for $260. How many hats?
questions.hint: Let h = hats. Then scarves = 25 − h.

teach.title: Mixtures, rates, and ages
text: For a mixture, the amount of pure substance is amount × percent. Use one equation for total amount and one for total pure substance.
For a boat in a current: downstream speed = boat + current, upstream speed = boat − current.
For ages, write each person's age now, then add the years later to each.

example.problem: Mix 10% and 30% solution to make 20 L of 22% solution.
steps: y = 12 L of the 30%, and x = 8 L of the 10%.

questions.prompt: Mix x L of 10% solution and y L of 30% solution to make 20 L of 22% solution. Which system fits?
questions.hint: Total pure amount = 0.22 × 20.
questions.solution: Total volume: x + y = 20. Pure substance: 0.10x + 0.30y = 0.22(20) = 4.4.

questions.prompt: Solve x + y = 20 and 0.10x + 0.30y = 4.4. How many litres of 30% solution are needed?
questions.hint: Put x = 20 − y into the second equation.

questions.prompt: A $3 per lb coffee is mixed with an $8 per lb coffee to make 20 lb worth $100 in all. How many pounds of the $8 coffee?
A boat goes 18 mph downstream and 10 mph upstream. What is its speed in still water, in mph?
questions.hint: b + c = 18 and b − c = 10. Add them.
questions.solution: Add: 2b = 28, so b = 14. (The current is 4 mph.)

questions.prompt: A boat goes 24 km downstream in 2 hours and 24 km back upstream in 3 hours. Which system gives the boat speed b and current c?
questions.hint: Speed = distance ÷ time for each trip.
questions.solution: Downstream speed: 24 ÷ 2 = 12, so b + c = 12. Upstream speed: 24 ÷ 3 = 8, so b − c = 8.

questions.prompt: Can you mix a 10% solution and a 30% solution to make a 35% solution?
choices: Yes, use more of the 30% solution
No, a mix must fall between 10% and 30%
No, 35 is not a multiple of 10
questions.hint: Think about what the mixture is made of.
questions.solution: A mixture of two solutions has a strength between the two. 35% is more than both, so it is impossible.

questions.prompt: $5000 is split between a 3% account and a 5% account. After one year the interest is $190. How many dollars are in the 5% account?
A father is 4 times as old as Ben. In 6 years he will be 3 times as old as Ben. How old is Ben now?
questions.hint: f = 4b. In 6 years: f + 6 = 3(b + 6).
questions.solution: 4b + 6 = 3(b + 6) = 3b + 18, so b = 12. The father is 48 (54 = 3 · 18 in 6 years).

teach.title: Systems of inequalities
text: A solution of a system of inequalities must make all of the inequalities true.
On a graph, it is the region where all the shadings overlap. A point is in it only if it passes every test.
Constraints like x ≥ 0 and y ≥ 0 keep the region in the top-right quarter.

example.problem: Is (2, 3) a solution of y > x and y ≤ 5?
steps: Both are true, so (2, 3) is in the region.

questions.prompt: Is (2, 3) a solution of y > x and y ≤ 5?
questions.hint: Test each inequality separately.
questions.solution: 3 > 2 is true and 3 ≤ 5 is true. It is in the region.

questions.prompt: Is (3, 3) a solution of x + y ≤ 6 and x − y > 1?
questions.hint: Test each inequality. Remember that > does not allow equal.
questions.solution: x + y = 6 ≤ 6 is true. x − y = 0 > 1 is false. So (3, 3) is not a solution.

questions.prompt: How many of the points (0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 0), (3, 3), (0, 2) satisfy both y ≤ x + 1 and y ≥ 1?
questions.hint: Test each point in both inequalities.
questions.solution: (0, 0): y ≥ 1 false. (1, 1): 1 ≤ 2 and 1 ≥ 1, true. (2, 0): false. (3, 3): 3 ≤ 4 and 3 ≥ 1, true. (0, 2): 2 ≤ 1 false. Two points.

questions.prompt: The region is x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, x + y ≤ 4. Which point is in it?
questions.hint: The point needs both coordinates at least 0 and a sum of 4 or less.

questions.prompt: Take x = 4 in x + y ≤ 10 and y ≥ 2x − 3. What is the largest whole number y that works?
questions.hint: The first gives y ≤ 10 − 4. The second gives y ≥ 2(4) − 3.
questions.solution: x + y ≤ 10 gives y ≤ 6. y ≥ 2(4) − 3 gives y ≥ 5. So y = 5 or 6, and the largest is 6.

questions.prompt: The boundary lines x + y = 4 and y = x cross. What is x at the crossing?
questions.hint: Substitute y = x into x + y = 4.
questions.solution: x + x = 4, so x = 2. The corner is (2, 2).

questions.prompt: A student works at most 20 hours a week (x hours tutoring, y hours at a cafe) and wants at least $200. Tutoring pays $15 an hour and the cafe pays $10 an hour. Which system fits?
questions.hint: "At most" is ≤ and "at least" is ≥. Match each pay rate to its hours.
questions.solution: Hours: x + y ≤ 20. Pay: 15x + 10y ≥ 200.

questions.prompt: Which point works for x + y ≤ 20 and 15x + 10y ≥ 200?
questions.hint: Test each point in both inequalities.

teach.title: Putting it together
text: Read the problem slowly: name your variables, write the equations, solve, and check in the words of the problem.
A feasible region is the overlap of all the constraint inequalities. Corner points are found where two boundary lines cross.

example.problem: Adult tickets cost $12 and child tickets cost $7. 150 tickets were sold for $1400. How many child tickets?

questions.prompt: Adult tickets cost $12 and child tickets cost $7. 150 tickets were sold for $1400. How many child tickets were sold?
questions.hint: a + c = 150 and 12a + 7c = 1400. Replace a with 150 − c.

questions.prompt: A jar has 30 coins, all quarters and dimes, worth $5.10. How many quarters?
questions.hint: Use cents: q + d = 30 and 25q + 10d = 510.

questions.prompt: How many litres of 50% acid must be mixed with 20% acid to make 30 L of 40% acid?
A rectangle has a length that is 2 more than twice its width. Its perimeter is 52. What is its width?
questions.hint: L = 2W + 2 and 2L + 2W = 52, so L + W = 26.
questions.solution: (2W + 2) + W = 26, so 3W = 24 and W = 8. The length is 18.

questions.prompt: Car A costs $30 plus $0.20 per mile. Car B costs $20 plus $0.30 per mile. For which distances is Car A cheaper?
questions.hint: Find where the costs are equal first. Then test a bigger distance.
questions.solution: Equal when 30 + 0.2m = 20 + 0.3m, so m = 100. At 200 miles A costs $70 and B costs $80, so A is cheaper for more than 100 miles.

questions.prompt: A shop spends $500 to set up and $4 per item. It sells each item for $9. How many items give break-even (cost = revenue)?
questions.hint: Cost is 500 + 4x. Revenue is 9x.

questions.prompt: The region is x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, 2x + y ≤ 10 and x + 2y ≤ 8. Which point is in it?
questions.hint: Test each point in 2x + y ≤ 10 and x + 2y ≤ 8.

questions.prompt: The boundary lines 2x + y = 10 and x + 2y = 8 cross at a corner of the region. What is its x-coordinate?
questions.hint: Multiply x + 2y = 8 by 2 so the x terms match, then subtract.
questions.solution: 2x + 4y = 16. Subtract 2x + y = 10: 3y = 6, so y = 2. Then 2x + 2 = 10, so x = 4.

teach.title: Ordered triples
text: A solution of a system in three variables is an ordered triple (x, y, z). It must make all three equations true.
